changed.what: Two acceptance criteria waited on beads that depend on this one (convention 7): compiling the preludes on trj (NVRTC) and on the Mac (Metal gateway) needs BD-015/BD-016's compile paths, and the on-device contraction detector is BD-017's probe; the implementer could never close BD-013 honestly. They now check what this bead delivers (both preludes expand K-selftest to byte-identical kernel text with zero lint findings; the detector text is lint-clean and the planted option sets are rejected by rule 4) and name BD-015, BD-016, BD-017, BD-020 and N21c-30 as the beads that run them on devices. The KA-525 note attributed BD-020's one-ulp plant to KA-525; its control is N21c-30:spark.contraction-prelude (BD-020's control B), corrected so the wrong control is not seeded.

Said --device all runs as one job once E1 is approved for gate:GATE-SPARK-07 (R11), without saying the call must cite that scope; under convention 14 an uncited call is adhoc (E0) and would still be refused 761. Added the cited form `frob spark fingerprint --device all --envelope-scope gate:GATE-SPARK-07 --key <k> --json` (or a launcher holding it).

FROB-REF-252's repairs were in the wrong order (Guarded first, Exact second) and lacked the third; N35-REF's row orders them Exact, Guarded, then non-strict requirement. Restated in the registry's order, so the refusal the implementer builds ranks its repairs as the registry does.

Applied F-U29a: snapshot_reads writes snapshots with `--telemetry T3 --snapshot-every 1` (without T3 the option is 802, N29ap1-02, and the step could not pass); N21b-26's own table already carries the same request. Applied F-U16b: added dep N16b-25 (owner of --tier beyond referee and --worlds on sim.run, M2; checked with graph_check, no cycle), since the first-light script runs `frob sim run --tier gpu-cuda ... --worlds 8192`.

Applied H-owners-3 and M1-6 (the mechanical R4-action finding was real): the verb paragraph still spelled eviction `--evict <key> | --evict-to <bytes> | --evict-all`, all 802 under NJL-01. Now the read forms (--list, --verify, exit 2 on corrupt) and the admin action `--action evict` with exactly one of `--entry <cache key>`, `--to-bytes <bytes>`, `--all`, no key, scope spark:admin, 802 for none/two/target without the action, 720 without the scope.

Applied F-U21b and the H-verbs-8 ANSWER; the C13-pending finding was real. nan_world and overflow now run through `frob sim run --conformance-plant <file>` with N21b-23's plant kinds `nan` (world 17, tick 100) and `overflow` (contacts, 40 against 32; 610 exit 6 under refuse) instead of the annex-test route and the 'requested of N21b-23' narration. Section 7 now states every command-line hook: --inject-faults, the two plant kinds, --inject-device-loss open|chunk=<k> (601), --inject-stall, no hook for over-budget (602 at admission), and `frob spark precompile <device> --unit <file> --key <k>` for 603.

The verb paragraph and the acceptance gave spark.place exit 0 or a refusal with exit 6 only; VERBS-spark's row gives exit 2 for a plan with findings (fallback under mixed-allowed, plan moved under prefer, stale check) and 247 (exit 3) for an unattainable --need-class. An implementer following the bead would return 0 for a fallback plan. Both places now carry the row's exit codes.

The unit test `kill_metal_rule` tested the KILL-METAL reading, whose decision function is N21b-08's (`kill_metal_rule_table`), and N21b-08 depends on this bead: BD-217 could not pass it without implementing the decision bead's function. Now `kill_metal_receipt_fields` (row 12's bound with pairs and threshold 0.25, and the Metal determinism result), the same form as the existing `kill_parity_receipt_fields`. The script ran every row as `frob sim run`, so: row 3 (PPO training) could not be measured at all; it is now `frob train start ... --task quad-flat-velocity --algo ppo --backend gpu-cuda --devices cuda:0 --worlds 8192 --steps <n> --seed <s> --key pr-3-... --json` (BD-198's trainer) with the rate read from `frob train status`. Row 2 now names its task (`--task quad-flat-velocity`), row 8 runs `--workload H:heightfield`, row 15 `--profile strict` (each otherwise measured a different row), and rows 13 and 14 add `--workers 24` and, because 24 threads exceed E0, cite R1 with `--envelope-scope gate:GATE-SPARK-03` (convention 14; uncited they are adhoc and refused 761; the choice of R1's scope is labelled DESIGN, see requests), logged `not run` without an approved R1.

Applied H-owners-3: the e2e note named the library listing `frob spark check --list`, the 802 form; now `--action list`, so the script's author is not pointed at a refused spelling.

The rewrites step ran `cargo test -p frob-kernels --test kernel_vectors -- --emit-digests <file>`; the default libtest harness rejects an unknown option after `--`, so the step could never produce its digests. Now `FROB_TEST_SEED=<seed> FROB_KERNEL_DIGESTS=<file> cargo test -p frob-kernels --test kernel_vectors`, with the test target stated as this bead's (it was defined nowhere).

Applied H-owners-3: the classes step of spark_probe.sh read `frob spark check --list --json` (802); now `--action list`, followed to the last page. FROB-REF-252's 'first repair: declare the kernel guarded or move the output to an exact kernel' inverted N35-REF's order; now exact kernel on quantized inputs, then guarded, then a non-strict requirement, the order the refusal's repairs must carry.

requests.what: R1 (incumbent and parity measurements on both cards and on all cores) admits the scopes gate:GATE-SPARK-21, gate:GATE-SPARK-03 and gate:GATE-SPARK-22, but none of them names the batch-cpu Performance rows 13 and 14 of §36.3 (24 threads on the M5 Ultra; BD-217, and N40-33 under the no-GPU variant), which are the only parity rows that need R1's all-cores clause; GATE-SPARK-03 is defined as the CUDA rows. BD-217 now cites `--envelope-scope gate:GATE-SPARK-03` for them (DESIGN). State in R1 that gate:GATE-SPARK-03 covers rows 13 and 14 of the parity campaign, or add the scope that does; otherwise an implementer of the envelope admission can read GATE-SPARK-03 as CUDA-only and refuse those runs 761, leaving rows 13 and 14 permanently `not run`.
